iterations.theme: Zlatko Krznarić: od obraćenja i fatalne nesreće do knjige 'Ti si svjedok' i poziva na trajni đakonat

sections.subtitle: Zaleđeni mostić i pitanje koje je promijenilo sve: „Bože, zašto?“
sections.screenshot_description: Zlatko Krznarić opisuje trenutak kad se, dužan i bez zdravlja, u bolnici pita „Bože, pa zašto?“
sections.content:
Epizoda podcasta Redefinicija počinje isječkom koji odmah pokazuje težinu priče. **Zlatko Krznarić** prepričava trenutak koji mu je preokrenuo život. Na jednom se zaleđenom mostiću njegov automobil zavrtio. Kad se zaustavio, isprva mu se ništa nije dogodilo. Tada je u njega udarila jedna gospođa i priklještila mu obje noge.

Ishod je bio težak. Desnu su mu nogu liječnici uspjeli „pokrpati“, a lijevu su morali amputirati. Krznarić opisuje kako se preko noći našao u bolnici *„dužan, slomljen, opljačkan, bez zdravlja“*. Postavio je pitanje koje si postavlja svatko pogođen tragedijom: **„Bože, pa zašto?“**

Tim isječkom voditelj uvodi slušatelje u razgovor o padu, predanju i novom početku. Naslov epizode to sažima ovako: fatalna nesreća bila je gostov novi početak.
sections.subtitle_en: An icy little bridge and the question that changed everything: “God, why?”
sections.screenshot_description_en: Zlatko Krznarić describes the moment when, in debt and without health, he asks in the hospital, “God, but why?”
sections.content_en:
The episode of the Redefinicija podcast begins with a clip that immediately shows the gravity of the story. **Zlatko Krznarić** recounts the moment that turned his life around. On an icy little bridge, his car spun around. When it stopped, at first nothing happened to him. Then a lady crashed into him and pinned both of his legs.

The outcome was severe. Doctors managed to “patch up” his right leg, but they had to amputate the left. Krznarić describes finding himself overnight in the hospital *“in debt, broken, robbed, without health”*. He asked the question that everyone struck by tragedy asks themselves: **“God, but why?”**

With that clip, the host introduces listeners to a conversation about the fall, surrender, and a new beginning. The title of the episode summarizes it like this: a fatal accident was the guest's new beginning.

sections.subtitle: Tko je Zlatko Krznarić? „Najprije dijete Božje“
sections.screenshot_description: Gost odgovara na voditeljevo pitanje „Tko je Zlatko Krznarić?“
sections.content:
Voditelj pozdravlja gosta riječima „Hvaljen Isus i Marija i sveti Josip!“ i predstavlja ga kao brata u Kristu. Zlatko Krznarić je katolički suprug, otac petero djece i vozač po zanimanju. Trenutno studira kako bi, ako Bog da, jednoga dana postao đakon. Prije razgovora o tom, kako ga sam gost naziva, „jako turbulentnom“ razdoblju, voditelj postavlja „filozofsko pitanje“: tko je zapravo Zlatko Krznarić?

Gost odgovara bez oklijevanja: *„Najprije dijete Božje. Na to sam ponosan.“* Zatim nabraja svoje uloge:

- otac,
- suprug,
- brat,
- i prije svega netko tko „želi ljubiti Gospodina“.

Sa suprugom **Sandrom**, koju naziva „najboljom ženom na svijetu“, oženjen je već 27 godina. Njihov obiteljski život opisuje kao „pun uspona i padova“, ali i pun vjernosti i ljubavi koja ih kroz sve to „diže uvijek“.
sections.subtitle_en: Who is Zlatko Krznarić? „First of all a child of God“
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest answers the host's question „Who is Zlatko Krznarić?“
sections.content_en:
The host greets the guest with the words „Praised be Jesus and Mary and Saint Joseph!“ and introduces him as a brother in Christ. Zlatko Krznarić is a Catholic husband, father of five children, and a driver by profession. He is currently studying so that, God willing, one day he might become a deacon. Before discussing that, as the guest himself calls it, „very turbulent“ period, the host asks a „philosophical question“: who actually is Zlatko Krznarić?

The guest answers without hesitation: *„First of all a child of God. I am proud of that.“* Then he lists his roles:

- father,
- husband,
- brother,
- and above all someone who „wants to love the Lord“.

He has already been married for 27 years to his wife **Sandra**, whom he calls the „best woman in the world“. He describes their family life as „full of ups and downs“, but also full of fidelity and love that through all of that „always lifts“ them.

sections.subtitle: Život bez Boga: tulumi, motor i sve dublja praznina
sections.screenshot_description: Gost opisuje osjećaj samoće i praznine u razdoblju bez Boga
sections.content:
Voditelj podsjeća da se život svakog obraćenika dijeli na dva dijela, prije i poslije susreta s Kristom, te pita kako je izgledao gostov život prije obraćenja.

Krznarić to naziva „klasikom“. Primio je sve sakramente na vrijeme, a onda je došao pubertet i vjera mu je postala „tlaka“. Godine 1993., s 21 godinom, **odbacio je Boga**. Počeo je razmišljati i živjeti svjetovno: tulumario je, aktivno se bavio sportom, imao vlastiti novac, auto i motor. Izvana je sve to, kaže, „lijepo izgledalo“.

Ta je faza trajala svega nekoliko mjeseci, otprilike pola godine. Uz svjetovni užitak sve je jače osjećao **samoću i prazninu**. Priznaje da je njegova vjera i ranije bila više „reda radi“, iz tradicije i odgoja, bez pravog žara. Ipak, ta mu je vjera očito značila mnogo, jer mu je bez nje „nešto falilo“.

Prekretnica je bila **velika ispovijed kod fra Ante Barišića** koja je trajala sat vremena. Kad je dobio odrješenje, s njega je, kako opisuje, „pao ogromno blato“ i izašao je „kao novi čovjek“. Od toga trenutka, kaže, nastoji živjeti „punim plućima za Gospodina“.
sections.subtitle_en: Life without God: parties, a motorbike, and an ever deeper emptiness
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest describes the feeling of loneliness and emptiness during the period without God
sections.content_en:
The host recalls that every convert's life is divided into two parts, before and after the encounter with Christ, and asks what the guest's life looked like before conversion.

Krznarić calls this a "classic." He received all the sacraments on time, and then puberty came and faith became a "drag" to him. In 1993, at 21 years old, **he rejected God**. He began to think and live worldly: he partied, actively engaged in sports, had his own money, a car, and a motorbike. From the outside all of that, he says, "looked nice."

That phase lasted only a few months, about half a year. Along with worldly pleasure, he felt **loneliness and emptiness** ever more strongly. He admits that even earlier his faith had been more "for form's sake," out of tradition and upbringing, without true fervor. Nevertheless, that faith obviously meant a lot to him, because without it "something was missing."

The turning point was **a major confession with fra Ante Barišić** that lasted an hour. When he received absolution, from him, as he describes, "huge mud fell" and he came out "as a new man." From that moment, he says, he strives to live "with full lungs for the Lord."

sections.subtitle: Sandra, „moj bingo“: kako je ponizno priznanje vratilo izgubljenu ljubav
sections.screenshot_description: Gost prepričava kako je Sandri došao „mali kao makovo zrno“ priznati pogrešku
sections.content:
Voditelj zatim pita za vezu koja je postojala prije te ispovijedi i nastavila se nakon nje. Krznarić kaže da je „veliki sretnik“ jer ima Sandru, ženu koja je od njega „učinila i oca i muža“ i uz koju se ostvario u mnogim područjima.

Njih su dvoje dvije godine hodali „na svjetovan način“, a onda ju je on ostavio. Bila je lijepa, pametna i dobra, ali on, kako priznaje, „nije imao žar“. Uslijedila je faza bez Boga u kojoj je imao druge djevojke.

Nakon ispovijedi napravio je „totalni reset“. Više nije izlazio, nego je usred dana odlazio na pola sata u crkvu na „čvenk s Gospodinom“ umjesto u kafić s društvom. Kroz duhovne obnove i molitvu shvatio je da je Sandra bila **najbolja osoba u njegovu životu**, njegov „bingo“.

Sandri je došao, kako sam kaže, *„kao najmanji od najmanjih, mali kao makovo zrno“*. Rekao joj je da je bio slijep i da je pogriješio. Dodao je da od nje ništa ne traži, pa ni da ga pozdravi ili ostane s njim u prijateljstvu, nego samo želi da to zna.

Sandra je u to vrijeme razlučivala hoće li postati časna sestra ili se udati. Čudila se njegovu dolasku jer je za nju „to bila završena priča“. Bojala se da je „lud“, iako ga je viđala u crkvi. S vremenom su ipak ponovno postali prijatelji, a zatim su opet počeli hodati. *„Ta se šansa isplatila“*, zaključuje Krznarić. Danas imaju petero djece, tri sina i dvije kćeri.
sections.subtitle_en: Sandra, "my bingo": how a humble confession brought back lost love
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest recounts how he came to Sandra "small as a poppy seed" to admit his mistake
sections.content_en:
The host then asks about the relationship that existed before that confession and continued after it. Krznarić says he is "a very lucky man" because he has Sandra, a woman who "made him both a father and a husband" and alongside whom he has realized himself in many areas.

The two of them dated for two years "in a worldly way", and then he left her. She was beautiful, smart, and good, but he, as he admits, "did not have the fire". A phase without God followed, in which he had other girlfriends.

After confession, he did a "total reset". He no longer went out, but in the middle of the day went for half an hour to church for a "date with the Lord" instead of to a café with friends. Through spiritual renewals and prayer, he realized that Sandra was **the best person in his life**, his "bingo".

He came to Sandra, as he himself says, *"as the smallest of the smallest, small as a poppy seed"*. He told her that he had been blind and that he had made a mistake. He added that he asked nothing of her, not even that she greet him or remain in friendship with him, but only wanted her to know that.

Sandra was at that time discerning whether to become a nun or get married. She was surprised by his arrival because for her "that was a finished story". She was afraid that he was "crazy", although she saw him in church. Over time, however, they became friends again, and then started dating again. *"That chance paid off"*, Krznarić concludes. Today they have five children, three sons and two daughters.

sections.subtitle: Tri godine u čistoći, brak 1998. i prijevara koja je odnijela sve
sections.screenshot_description: Gost opisuje kako ih je investitor na Krku prevario i kako je ostao bez svega
sections.content:
Krznarić naglašava pojedinost koju voditelj spominje: sa Sandrom je **tri godine hodao u čistoći**. Prije su, kaže, „probali sve što svijet nudi“ i shvatili da „to nije to“. U čistoći je otkrio njezinu unutarnju ljepotu. To je ono „od čega se živi“, „ono što traje“, korijen i temelj na koji se kasnije može osloniti, jer je tu savez između Boga i njih dvoje.

Vjenčali su se **1998. godine**. Život se razvijao lijepo: posao, obitelj, sve je „išlo super“. Krznarić je sa skupinom ulagača sav novac uložio u gradnju nekretnina. Prva zgrada na **Pagu** donijela je lijepu zaradu. Sljedeći projekt na **Krku** završio je katastrofom jer ih je, kako kaže, jedan čovjek prevario i ostali su bez svega.

Detalje naziva „kompliciranom pričom“ i ne ulazi u njih. Opisuje samo svoje stanje: s 39 godina osjećao se *„opljačkan, dužan, prevaren“*.
sections.subtitle_en: Three years in purity, marriage in 1998, and a fraud that took everything away
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest describes how an investor on Krk defrauded them and how he was left with nothing
sections.content_en:
Krznarić emphasizes a detail mentioned by the host: with Sandra, he **dated in purity for three years**. Before, he says, they had "tried everything the world offers" and realized that "that was not it." In purity, he discovered her inner beauty. That is what "one lives on," "what lasts," the root and foundation one can rely on later, because there is a covenant between God and the two of them.

They married in **1998**. Life was developing nicely: work, family, everything was "going great." Krznarić invested all the money with a group of investors into real estate construction. The first building on **Pag** brought a nice profit. The next project on **Krk** ended in a catastrophe because, as he says, one man defrauded them and they were left with nothing.

He calls the details a "complicated story" and does not go into them. He only describes his state: at 39 years old, he felt *"robbed, in debt, defrauded"*.

sections.subtitle: Stečaj, a tri tjedna kasnije nesreća kilometar od kuće
sections.screenshot_description: Gost prepričava nesreću na zaleđenom mostiću 2011. godine
sections.content:
Nevolje su se nizale. Nakon prijevare uslijedio je **stečaj**, a dva do tri tjedna kasnije, 2011. godine, Krznarić je doživio prometnu nesreću. Dogodila se samo kilometar od kuće, na cesti kojom se vozio svakodnevno i na kojoj je „napamet znao svaki kamen“.

Na zaleđenom mostiću automobil se zavrtio, a kad se zaustavio, u njega je udarila gospođa i priklještila mu obje noge. Desna je spašena, a **lijeva je amputirana**.

U bolnici je, kako opisuje, bio „dužan, slomljen, opljačkan, bez zdravlja“. Pitao je: *„Bože, pa zašto? Bože, gdje si? Zašto si dopustio sve ovo tako odjedanput? Sa svih strana me tučeš.“* Sve se dogodilo iznenada, a on tri dana nije mogao spavati.
sections.subtitle_en: Bankruptcy, and three weeks later an accident a kilometer from home
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest recounts the accident on an icy small bridge in 2011
sections.content_en:
Troubles followed one after another. After the fraud followed **bankruptcy**, and two to three weeks later, in 2011, Krznarić suffered a traffic accident. It happened only a kilometer from home, on the road he drove on daily and on which he „knew every stone by heart“.

On the icy small bridge the car spun around, and when it stopped, a lady crashed into him and pinned both of his legs. The right one was saved, and **the left one was amputated**.

In the hospital, as he describes, he was „in debt, broken, robbed, without health“. He asked: *„God, why? God, where are you? Why did you allow all this so all at once? You are striking me from all sides.“* Everything happened suddenly, and he could not sleep for three days.

sections.subtitle: „Ja bum ga rodila“: Sandrina vjera kao planina
sections.screenshot_description: Gost s emocijom prenosi Sandrine riječi o trudnoći s petim djetetom
sections.content:
Krznarić se osjećao slomljeno i, kako kaže, kao u „pat poziciji“: nije se imao za što primiti i bio je satjeran u kut. Tada mu je u bolnicu došla supruga i rekla: *„Zlatko, trudna sam dva mjeseca s našim petim djetetom, s našim Leom.“*

Financijska slika bila je teška. On je jedini zarađivao, a Sandra je bila kućanica. Imali su kredit u švicarskim francima, za koji voditelj ironično dobacuje da je bio „jako isplativ“. Pod hipotekom su bile i njihova kuća i kuća njegovih roditelja. Čak i da se Sandra zaposlila, ne bi bilo dovoljno za ratu.

Tada ga je Sandra primila za ruku i rekla:

> *„Evo, taman da smo sad tak siromašni da nikada više nećemo ništa imati i da nam zbog našeg siromaštva socijalna služba mora to dijete uzeti, ja bum ga rodila. Ja sam mu majka. Dala bum mu život jer Bog ima plan za nas.“*

Krznarić kaže da mu je upravo to bilo „najpotrebnije“. U njoj je vidio hrabrost, odanost i vjeru koja je bila „planina“, i to ga je silno ohrabrilo.
sections.subtitle_en: "I will give birth to him": Sandra's faith like a mountain
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest emotionally conveys Sandra's words about her pregnancy with their fifth child
sections.content_en:
Krznarić felt broken and, as he says, in a "stalemate": he had nothing to hold on to and was backed into a corner. Then his wife came to the hospital and told him: *"Zlatko, I am two months pregnant with our fifth child, with our Leo."*

The financial picture was difficult. He was the sole earner, and Sandra was a homemaker. They had a loan in Swiss francs, which the host ironically quips was "very profitable". Both their house and his parents' house were mortgaged. Even if Sandra had found a job, it would not have been enough for the installment.

Then Sandra took his hand and said:

> *"Look, even if we are so poor now that we will never have anything again and that because of our poverty social services have to take that child away from us, I will give birth to him. I am his mother. I will give him life because God has a plan for us."*

Krznarić says that this was precisely what was "most needed" for him. In her he saw courage, loyalty, and a faith that was a "mountain", and that encouraged him immensely.

sections.subtitle: Kapelan koji se smijao: „To je prava stvar!“
sections.screenshot_description: Gost prenosi proročke riječi bolničkog kapelana vlč. Milana Lončarića
sections.content:
Ubrzo ga je posjetio bolnički kapelan, **vlč. Milan Lončarić**. Krznarić mu je nabrajao svoje nevolje, a kapelan se, na njegovo čuđenje, sve više smijao. Kad mu je rekao da mu osiguravatelj nije stigao uplatiti kasko policu od oko dva i pol milijuna kuna, pa je ostao bez ičega, svećenik je uzviknuo: *„To je prava stvar!“*

Krznarić se pitao je li kapelan „normalan“. Tada je čuo riječi koje danas naziva **proročkima**:

> *„Zlatko, do sad si mogao biti katolik na papiru, ali, evo, danas te Bog zove da mu predaš svoj život. Ako si to spreman učiniti, pisat ćeš o njemu, svjedočit ćeš. Imat ćeš pravu radost koja ne visi o tvome novcu i zdravlju.“*

Kapelan mu je kasnije priznao da uopće nije bio svjestan što govori, a Krznarić je uvjeren da ga je tada obuzeo Duh Sveti. Otišao je u bolničku kapelicu i **predao svoj život Bogu**. Spustio se na njega, kaže, „predivan mir“, kao da je s Bogom sklopio najvažniji ugovor „bez tinte i papira“.

Kasnije se sve posložilo „na najbolji mogući način“. Uz Božju pomoć, kako kaže „na nadnaravan način“, obitelj je odavno vratila sve dugove. *„Danas sam sretan čovjek. Bog je živ“*, poručuje.
sections.subtitle_en: The chaplain who laughed: “That is the real thing!”
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest conveys the prophetic words of the hospital chaplain vlč. Milan Lončarić
sections.content_en:
Soon he was visited by the hospital chaplain, **vlč. Milan Lončarić**. Krznarić listed his troubles to him, and the chaplain, to his astonishment, laughed more and more. When he told him that the insurer had not managed to pay out his comprehensive insurance policy of about two and a half million kunas, so he was left with nothing, the priest exclaimed: *“That is the real thing!”*

Krznarić wondered whether the chaplain was “normal”. Then he heard words that he today calls **prophetic**:

> *“Zlatko, until now you could be a Catholic on paper, but, behold, today God is calling you to surrender your life to Him. If you are ready to do that, you will write about Him, you will testify. You will have true joy that does not hang on your money and health.”*

The chaplain later admitted to him that he was not at all aware of what he was saying, and Krznarić is convinced that the Holy Spirit seized him then. He went to the hospital chapel and **surrendered his life to God**. A “wonderful peace,” he says, descended upon him, as if he had concluded the most important contract with God “without ink and paper”.

Later, everything fell into place “in the best possible way”. With God's help, as he says “in a supernatural way”, the family long ago repaid all debts. *“Today I am a happy man. God is alive”*, he shares.

sections.subtitle: „Ti si svjedok“: knjiga koju najlošiji učenik dvije godine nije htio napisati
sections.screenshot_description: Gost opisuje svoju borbu s poticajem „Napiši knjigu!“
sections.content:
Kapelanove riječi su se obistinile. Godine **2017.** izašla je Krznarićeva prva knjiga, **„Ti si svjedok“**. Voditelj je naziva uspješnicom s kojom je autor obišao cijelu državu i šire te tvrdi da se nalazi „u gotovo svakom katoličkom domu“. I sam ima primjerak s autorovim potpisom, ali ga je zaboravio ponijeti na snimanje.

Krznarić se najprije javno zahvaljuje voditelju što mu je napravio **lekturu** i šali se da zbog toga kod Gospodina ide „među svece i mučenike“. Voditelj odgovara da je „bilo posla, ali bio je gušt“. Gost pritom sebe naziva „polupismenim“.

Priznaje da kapelanovo „pisat ćeš o njemu“ isprva nije shvatio ozbiljno. Nakon nekog vremena, kad je u crkvi pitao Boga što može učiniti za njega, dobio je odgovor: *„Napiši knjigu!“* Slijedila je borba duga nešto manje od dvije godine. Bio je, kaže, jedan od najgorih učenika u školi i nije mogao zamisliti da sjedne za stol i piše. Pitao se i tko bi to uopće čitao.

Rezultat ga je iznenadio: knjiga je imala **četiri izdanja, prodana je u tisućama primjeraka i prevedena je**. Vjeruje da je čitateljima dirnula iskrenost. U knjizi je, kaže, „ogolio sebe do kraja“, pišući o slabostima, svađama i intimi. *„Svi smo negdje tanki, svi imamo nešto što nas žulja“*, objašnjava. Nije želio pisati ništa veliko o sebi, nego koliko je on slab, a Bog velik kroz njegove slabosti. Bog je, kaže, uvijek vjeran, a pitanje je samo jesmo li mi.
sections.subtitle_en: "You Are a Witness": a book that the worst student did not want to write for two years
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest describes his struggle with the prompting "Write a book!"
sections.content_en:
The chaplain's words came true. In the year **2017**, Krznarić's first book, **"You Are a Witness"**, came out. The host calls it a bestseller with which the author toured the entire country and beyond, claiming that it is found "in almost every Catholic home." He himself has a copy with the author's signature, but forgot to bring it to the recording.

Krznarić first publicly thanks the host for doing the **proofreading** for him and jokes that because of this, with the Lord he goes "among the saints and martyrs." The host replies that there "was work, but it was a pleasure." The guest at the same time calls himself "semi-literate."

He admits that he did not take the chaplain's "you will write about him" seriously at first. After some time, when he asked God in church what he could do for Him, he received the answer: *"Write a book!"* A struggle lasting a little less than two years followed. He was, he says, one of the worst students in school and could not imagine sitting down at a table and writing. He also wondered who would even read it.

The result surprised him: the book had **four editions, was sold in thousands of copies, and was translated**. He believes that the honesty touched the readers. In the book, he says, he "stripped himself down completely," writing about weaknesses, quarrels, and intimacy. *"We are all thin somewhere, we all have something that rubs us,"* he explains. He did not want to write anything great about himself, but rather how weak he is, and how great God is through his weaknesses. God is, he says, always faithful, and the only question is whether we are.

sections.subtitle: Olovka u Božjim rukama i tiskar koji ne vjeruje nakladama
sections.screenshot_description: Gost prepričava kako nije prepoznao vlastiti tekst kad ga je svećenik čitao
sections.content:
Na pitanje o najdražem poglavlju Krznarić govori o samom procesu pisanja. Često nije mogao dovršiti zaključak svjedočanstva, nekoliko završnih rečenica, sve dok mu nakon molitve i predanja nisu „došle riječi“.

Jednom ga je svećenik pozvao u župu da svjedoči i pročitao ulomak iz njegove knjige. Krznarić je slušao i mislio: *„Gle, kak je ovo lijepo rekao!“* Tek je poslije shvatio da je to njegov tekst. Zaboravio ga je jer, kako kaže, „nije bilo moje“. Zahvaljuje Bogu „na suradnji“ i na nadahnuću.

Zabavna je i priča o tiskaru. Kad je pitao Boga koliko primjeraka tiskati, dobivao je brojke od nekoliko tisuća. Vlasnik tiskare, nevjernik, čudio se: *„Tko si ti?“* Krznarić mu je odgovorio da je „nitko i ništa“, ali da Onaj koji ga je potaknuo „drži svijet u ruci“.

I danas tiska kod istog čovjeka. Tiskar se, kaže, nije obratio, ali mu govori: *„Ti nisi uračunljiv, ti si van svih standarda.“* Pred petim izdanjem Krznarić se opet „boji pitati“ Boga za brojku. Sebe opisuje kao „samo olovku u Njegovim rukama“.
sections.subtitle_en: A pencil in God's hands and a printer who does not believe the print runs
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest recounts how he did not recognize his own text when a priest read it
sections.content_en:
To the question about his favorite chapter, Krznarić speaks about the very process of writing. Often he could not complete the conclusion of a testimony, a few final sentences, until after prayer and surrender "the words came" to him.

Once a priest invited him to a parish to give a testimony and read an excerpt from his book. Krznarić listened and thought: *"Look, how beautifully he said this!"* Only later did he realize that it was his own text. He had forgotten it because, as he says, "it wasn't mine." He thanks God "for the collaboration" and for the inspiration.

The story about the printer is also entertaining. When he asked God how many copies to print, he received numbers of several thousand. The print shop owner, a non-believer, was astonished: *"Who are you?"* Krznarić replied to him that he was "nobody and nothing," but that the One who prompted him "holds the world in His hand."

Even today he prints with the same man. The printer, he says, has not converted, but tells him: *"You are not sane, you are beyond all standards."* Before the fifth edition, Krznarić is again "afraid to ask" God for the number. He describes himself as "just a pencil in His hands."

sections.subtitle: Napad na molitelje i molitva koja je slomila agresivno srce
sections.screenshot_description: Gost objašnjava zašto je zajednica odlučila moliti za čovjeka koji ga je napao
sections.content:
Voditeljevo najdraže svjedočanstvo iz knjige vezano je uz inicijativu **„40 dana za život“**. Krznarić je bio na ručku kod majke, juha je već bila u tanjuru, kad je osjetio poticaj da izađe van. *„Gospodine, pa jedem, kaj sad?“* pitao je, ali je izašao.

Pred molitelje je automobilom došao čovjek i počeo ih agresivno vrijeđati. Krznarić ga je počeo snimati mobitelom. Kad je čovjek to primijetio, pitao ga je tko je i zašto snima, a zatim ga je **počeo daviti**. Krznarić se oslobodio, napadač je otišao, a policija je napravila očevid jer se napad dogodio na javnom mjestu.

Zajednica je potom odlučila **moliti za napadača**. U tome Krznarić vidi „poantu Božje pedagogije“: nisu uzvratili, nisu išli „na mišiće“, nego „na Božji način“. Nakon nekog vremena čovjek je župniku uplatio prilog za crkvu, nazvao Krznarića i zamolio ga za oprost. *„Njegovo srce se slomilo. Ono agresivno počelo je biti ljudsko, počelo je biti Božje“*, kaže. Taj događaj naziva „prstom Božjim“ i zato ga je uvrstio u knjigu.
sections.subtitle_en: Attack on those praying and the prayer that broke an aggressive heart
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest explains why the community decided to pray for the man who attacked him
sections.content_en:
The host's favorite testimony from the book is related to the **"40 Days for Life"** initiative. Krznarić was having lunch at his mother's, the soup was already in the plate, when he felt an impulse to go outside. *"Lord, but I am eating, what now?"* he asked, but he went out.

A man arrived by car in front of those praying and began to aggressively insult them. Krznarić began recording him with his cell phone. When the man noticed this, he asked him who he was and why he was recording, and then **began to choke him**. Krznarić broke free, the attacker left, and the police conducted an on-site investigation because the attack took place in a public place.

The community then decided to **pray for the attacker**. In this, Krznarić sees the "point of God's pedagogy": they did not retaliate, they did not go "by muscle", but "in God's way". After some time, the man paid a donation for the church to the parish priest, called Krznarić, and asked him for forgiveness. *"His heart broke. That which was aggressive began to be human, began to be God's"*, he says. He calls this event "the finger of God" and that is why he included it in the book.

sections.subtitle: Govor na prvoj pričesti i neočekivani poziv: „Redimo te za đakona“
sections.screenshot_description: Gost prepričava reakciju župnika i kapelana nakon govora na sinovoj prvoj pričesti
sections.content:
Voditelj primjećuje da Krznarića posljednje četiri godine gotovo nema u javnosti i pita gdje je bio. Odgovor glasi: **dobio je poziv za trajnog đakona.**

Nije ni znao da trajni đakonat postoji niti ga je to ikad zanimalo. Kad mu je sin išao na prvu pričest, župnik je tražio nekoga od roditelja da održi govor. Nitko se nije javio, pa je župnik rekao: „Ajde, budeš ti, Zlatko.“ Govorio je „po Duhu“, a čim je završio, prišli su mu kapelan i župnik: *„Redimo te za đakona!“*

Nasmijao se i rekao im neka rede nekog drugog. No u molitvi mu se ta misao stalno vraćala. Nije znao da oženjen čovjek može služiti blizu oltara, pa se počeo raspitivati.

U razgovoru navodi da je jedan od najpoznatijih đakona **sveti Franjo**, koji se iz poniznosti nije usudio postati svećenikom. Za oženjenog kandidata postoje ovi uvjeti:

- mora biti stariji od 35 godina,
- supruga mora dati pristanak,
- mora završiti **pet godina teološkog studija**.

Prva dva uvjeta nisu bila problem, ali treći ga je prestrašio: *„Ma koji faks? Pa nikad nisam bio za školu!“*
sections.subtitle_en: Speech at First Communion and an Unexpected Calling: "We Are Ordaining You as a Deacon"
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest recounts the reaction of the parish priest and the parochial vicar after the speech at his son's First Communion
sections.content_en:
The host notes that Krznarić has hardly been in the public eye for the last four years and asks where he has been. The answer is: **he received a calling to the permanent diaconate.**

He did not even know that the permanent diaconate existed, nor had he ever been interested in it. When his son went to First Communion, the parish priest asked for one of the parents to give a speech. No one volunteered, so the parish priest said: "Come on, you will do it, Zlatko." He spoke "according to the Spirit," and as soon as he finished, the parochial vicar and the parish priest approached him: *"We are ordaining you as a deacon!"*

He laughed and told them to ordain someone else. But in prayer, that thought kept returning to him. He did not know that a married man could serve near the altar, so he began to inquire.

In the conversation, he states that one of the most famous deacons is **Saint Francis**, who out of humility did not dare to become a priest. For a married candidate, these conditions exist:

- he must be older than 35 years,
- his wife must give consent,
- he must complete **five years of theological studies**.

The first two conditions were not a problem, but the third one scared him: *"What college? Why, I was never one for school!"*

sections.subtitle: 580 kilometara na biciklu, s protezom, do Međugorja
sections.screenshot_description: Gost se smije prepričavajući traktor koji ga je štitio od vjetra
sections.content:
Kako bi razlučio poziv, Krznarić je odlučio „ući u ring“ s Bogom. Biciklom je krenuo iz **Čakovca u Međugorje**, oko 580 kilometara. Planirao je usput izmoliti tisuću Zdravo Marija i „podvući crtu“. Nije isplanirao ni rutu ni noćenja, bio je bez kondicije i pripreme, s jednom zdravom nogom i jednom protezom, i potpuno se predao providnosti. Na putu se dogodilo nekoliko zgoda koje naziva „Božjim anegdotama“:

- **Traktor u zavjetrini.** Na putu prema Karlovcu skrenuo je do svetišta blaženog Alojzija Stepinca u Krašiću, gdje nikad nije bio. Pukla mu je guma, a krpanje malom pumpom dugo je trajalo. Zamolio je Boga da mu pošalje traktor koji bi mu bio zavjetrina. Na Dan domovinske zahvalnosti, neradni dan, pred njim se pojavio traktor s prikolicom. Vozio se za njim desetak kilometara i supruzi poslao fotografiju.
- **Soba s Gospinom slikom.** U Slunju je sve bilo zauzeto i skupo. Zavapio je: „Marijo, pa ja k tebi idem, kaj sad tu spavam u nekom kanalu?“ Prišla mu je jedna ženica i ponudila smještaj, malu i jeftinu sobu s velikom Gospinom slikom na sredini.
- **Pumpa kod Plitvica.** Kad mu je kod Plitvičkih jezera ponovno pukla guma, poželio je veliku pumpu. Policajac ga je uputio na samoposlužni servis za bicikle odmah preko puta.
- **Biciklist s krunicom.** Ostao je bez rezervne gume u kraju bez trgovina. Na cesti je zatekao biciklista koji ga je ranije prestigao, a sada se odmarao. Kad mu je Krznarić rekao da ide u Međugorje, čovjek mu je pokazao krunicu i poklonio zračnicu točno potrebne dimenzije.
sections.subtitle_en: 580 kilometers on a bicycle, with a prosthesis, to Međugorje
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest laughs as he recounts the tractor that shielded him from the wind
sections.content_en:
In order to discern his calling, Krznarić decided to "enter the ring" with God. He set off by bicycle from **Čakovec to Međugorje**, about 580 kilometers. He planned to pray a thousand Hail Marys along the way and "draw a line". He had planned neither the route nor overnight stays, he was without fitness and preparation, with one healthy leg and one prosthesis, and he completely surrendered himself to providence. Along the way, several events occurred that he calls "God's anecdotes":

- **A tractor in the slipstream.** On the way toward Karlovac, he turned off to the shrine of Blessed Alojzije Stepinac in Krašić, where he had never been before. His tire blew out, and patching it with a small pump took a long time. He asked God to send him a tractor that would serve as a windbreak for him. On Homeland Thanksgiving Day, a non-working day, a tractor with a trailer appeared before him. He rode behind it for about ten kilometers and sent a photograph to his wife.
- **A room with Our Lady's picture.** In Slunj, everything was booked and expensive. He cried out: "Mary, but I am going to you, why am I sleeping here in some ditch now?" A little woman approached him and offered accommodation, a small and cheap room with a large picture of Our Lady in the middle.
- **A pump near Plitvice.** When his tire blew out again near Plitvička jezera, he wished for a large pump. A police officer directed him to a self-service bicycle repair station right across the street.
- **A cyclist with a Rosary.** He was left without a spare tire in an area without shops. On the road, he came across a cyclist who had overtaken him earlier and was now resting. When Krznarić told him that he was going to Međugorje, the man showed him a Rosary and gave him an inner tube of the exact required dimensions.

sections.subtitle: „Bože, zar si pozvao mene?“ i odgovor na Podbrdu
sections.screenshot_description: Gost prenosi odgovor koji je u tišini čuo na Podbrdu
sections.content:
U Međugorju je sudjelovao na susretu za obitelji koji organizira **Robert Rukavina**. Žuta dvorana bila je prepuna, prema gostovoj procjeni s 500 do 600 ljudi. Misu je predvodio **fra Petar Ljubičić**. Sandra je znala da se suprug muči s đakonatom i da ga ne želi prihvatiti.

Kod pričesti je fra Petar pitao ima li netko dopuštenje da bude izvanredni djelitelj pričesti. Nitko se nije javio, a zbor je zapjevao: *„Bože, zar si pozvao mene?“* i *„Znam da zoveš, al' se bojim.“* Krznariću su navrle suze, a Sandra mu je šapnula: *„Vidiš, vidiš što propuštaš?“* Odgovorio joj je: „Pusti me.“

Popeo se na **Podbrdo**, do plavog križa, i jadao se Gospi da nije za fakultet i da je toliko zaboravljiv da ne zna zašto je otišao u garažu. Kad je utihnuo i zamolio je da mu odgovori, u tišini je čuo: *„Čekat ću te dok ne prihvatiš poziv.“* Njegova reakcija bila je kratka: *„Joj, užas.“*
sections.subtitle_en: “God, did you call me?” and the answer on Podbrdo
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest conveys the answer he heard in silence on Podbrdo
sections.content_en:
In Međugorje, he took part in a gathering for families organized by **Robert Rukavina**. The Yellow Hall was packed, according to the guest's estimate with 500 to 600 people. The Mass was celebrated by **fra Petar Ljubičić**. Sandra knew that her husband was struggling with the diaconate and that he did not want to accept it.

At Communion, fra Petar asked if anyone had permission to be an extraordinary minister of Holy Communion. No one came forward, and the choir began to sing: *“God, did you call me?”* and *“I know you are calling, but I am afraid.”* Tears welled up in Krznarić's eyes, and Sandra whispered to him: *“You see, you see what you are missing?”* He answered her: “Leave me alone.”

He climbed up to **Podbrdo**, to the blue cross, and lamented to Our Lady that he was not cut out for college and that he was so forgetful that he did not know why he went to the garage. When he fell silent and asked her to answer him, in the silence he heard: *“I will wait for you until you accept the call.”* His reaction was brief: *“Oh, terrible.”*

sections.subtitle: Klanjanje, monfortanac i biskup kao „drugo mišljenje“
sections.screenshot_description: Gost objašnjava kako je od biskupa očekivao da će ga osloboditi poziva
sections.content:
Poticaji su se nastavili. Krznarić u župi četvrtkom vodi meditaciju na klanjanju dok prijatelj **Aleks** svira gitaru. Jednom je okupljene pozvao da se predaju Bogu „svim srcem, svom snagom, svom dušom, bez kalkulacije“. U istom trenutku čuo je unutarnji glas: *„Čekam te da mi se predaš, kao što govoriš drugima.“* Rasplakao se, a Aleksu, koji ga je pitao što mu je, odgovorio je samo neka svira.

Zatim je zamolio za molitvu monfortanca **vlč. Zrinka**, kojeg opisuje kao svećenika s darom spoznanja. Ništa mu nije otkrio osim da ima „muku s Gospodinom“. Svećenik je u molitvi rekao: *„Imaš poziv. Gospodin te zove, pogledaj u njega, budi hrabar, kreni, ne boj se.“* Krznarić priznaje da je priželjkivao da mu netko kaže „ne trebaš“, a događalo se upravo suprotno.

Kad je shvatio da „bježi od samoga sebe“, otišao je varaždinskom biskupu **Boži Radošu**. Nadao se da će ga crkveni autoritet osloboditi. Voditelj to duhovito naziva „mišljenjem drugog doktora“. Biskup je, međutim, odgovorio: *„Pa super, bilo bi lijepo da krenete.“* *„Gotovo je, sad stvarno moram“*, zaključio je tada Krznarić.
sections.subtitle_en: Eucharistic adoration, a Montfortian, and a bishop as a „second opinion“
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest explains how he expected the bishop to release him from the calling
sections.content_en:
The promptings continued. Krznarić leads meditation at Eucharistic adoration in the parish on Thursdays while his friend **Aleks** plays guitar. Once, he called on those gathered to surrender to God „with all their heart, with all their strength, with all their soul, without calculation“. At the same moment, he heard an inner voice: *„I am waiting for you to surrender to Me, as you tell others.“* He burst into tears, and to Aleks, who asked him what was wrong with him, he only replied to just play.

Then he asked for prayer from the Montfortian **vlč. Zrinko**, whom he describes as a priest with the gift of knowledge. He revealed nothing to him except that he had a „struggle with the Lord“. The priest said in prayer: *„You have a calling. The Lord is calling you, look at Him, be courageous, set out, do not be afraid.“* Krznarić admits that he wished someone would tell him „you don't have to“, and exactly the opposite was happening.

When he realized that he was „running away from himself“, he went to the bishop of Varaždin **Bože Radoš**. He hoped that church authority would release him. The host wittily calls this „the opinion of a second doctor“. The bishop, however, replied: *„Well great, it would be nice for you to set out.“* *„It's over, now I really must“*, Krznarić concluded then.

sections.subtitle: „Prestar sam za faks“ i kapelica pokraj Jordanovca
sections.screenshot_description: Gost govori o kapelici trajnog klanjanja pokraj fakulteta na Jordanovcu
sections.content:
Ostao mu je još jedan izgovor: godine. *„Tko je vidio s 50 godina ići na faks?“* govorio je Bogu. Nekoliko dana kasnije jedna mu je gospođa rekla da su to „prave godine“, jer je njezin otac teologiju upisao s 55 i završio je sa 60 i nešto. Krznarić je pomislio da je taj „još luđi“. Na svaki njegov pokušaj bijega, kaže, Bog mu je na put stavljao ljude koji su mu poručivali: „Ja sam to odlučio, ja te vodim.“

Upisao se na isusovački fakultet na **Jordanovcu**. Ondje mu je najdraže to što se pokraj fakulteta nalazi **kapelica trajnog klanjanja**. Klanjanje silno voli. U njegovoj župi u **Nedelišću** jednom mjesečno održava se cjelodnevno klanjanje i on tada ostaje od početka do kraja, a ako je radni dan, uzima godišnji odmor. *„Ne možemo bolje iskoristiti vrijeme nego biti u Božjoj prisutnosti“*, kaže. Na fakultetu uvijek „prvo dođe Isusu, on je glavni“, a tek onda „ovim zemaljskima“, profesorima.
sections.subtitle_en: „I am too old for college“ and the chapel next to Jordanovac
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest speaks about the perpetual adoration chapel next to the faculty on Jordanovac
sections.content_en:
He had one excuse left: age. *„Who ever heard of going to college at 50?“* he said to God. A few days later, a lady told him that it was the „right age“, because her father enrolled in theology at 55 and finished it in his sixties. Krznarić thought that that man was „even crazier“. At his every attempt to flee, he says, God placed people in his path who told him: „I decided this, I am leading you.“

He enrolled at the Jesuit faculty on **Jordanovac**. What he likes most there is that next to the faculty is a **chapel of perpetual adoration**. He loves Eucharistic adoration immensely. In his parish in **Nedelišće**, an all-day Eucharistic adoration is held once a month and he stays from beginning to end, and if it is a workday, he takes annual leave. *„We cannot make better use of time than to be in God's presence“*, he says. At the faculty, he always „comes to Jesus first, He is the main one“, and only then to „these earthly ones“, the professors.

sections.subtitle: Ispiti pred Presvetim: petica, pet pitanja i test koji nije podijeljen
sections.screenshot_description: Gost prepričava kako se profesor predomislio i umjesto pismenog ispita ga ispitao usmeno
sections.content:
Krznarić je sada na četvrtoj godini. Položio je hebrejski, latinski, grčki i „sve te filozofije“. Naglašava da ne govori „racionalno“, nego iz odnosa s Bogom, i iznosi niz zgoda s ispita:

- **Psihologija kod patera Mije Nikića.** Pred Presvetim je rekao: „Ako je to od tebe poziv, dobit ću peticu, i to mi je znak da si ti sa mnom.“ Profesor ga je pitao upravo ono što je najbolje znao i na kraju rekao: „Kad bi bar redoviti studenti ovako dobro učili!“
- **Srednjovjekovna filozofija.** Literatura su bile dvije knjige po 500 stranica sitnog tiska, koje mu je Sandra donijela iz knjižnice, i skripta od stotinjak stranica. Večer prije ispita htio je ponavljati, ali je u molitvi osjetio poziv: „Idi na svetu misu u znak zahvale za ispit koji bi sutra prošao.“ Otišao je. Sutradan mu je pred učionicom nepoznati student nabrojio pet pitanja koja profesor obično postavlja. Upravo su ta pitanja došla na ispitu, a tog studenta nikad više nije vidio.
- **Sociologija kod profesora Peračkovića.** Bojao se pismenog dijela s 30 do 40 pitanja nakon kojeg slijedi usmeni. Pred Presvetim je molio da ga profesor ispita samo usmeno. Profesor je na ispitu podigao test, gledao ga, spustio ga i rekao: „Predomislio sam se, pitat ću vas usmeno.“ Dobio je desetku. Sutradan mu je profesor napisao e-mail da je ponio test, „ali ga nije mogao dati“. Krznarić mu je odgovorio da je upravo za to molio, a na kraju su razmijenili knjige.
- **Moralna teologija.** Prije dva tjedna izašao je na ispit nedovoljno pripremljen, jer je dan ranije svjedočio u jednoj župi, a skriptu sa sitnim slovima slabo je vidio. Zadihan je stigao biciklom, nakon što ga je izvadio iz kamiona, i ušao s pet odlikaša. Ispit je trajao oko sat vremena. Dobio je osmicu, a profesor mu je rekao: „Vi ste najviše govorili po duhu.“ Kolege su to primijetile, a on je to doživio kao potvrdu.

Uz to se nasmijao i opisu svoje rutine: navečer kamionom vozi do Zagreba, ponavlja gradivo u tišini, a onda „kao pravi student“ biciklom odlazi na fakultet.
sections.subtitle_en: Exams before the Blessed Sacrament: a five, five questions, and a test that was not handed out
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest recounts how the professor changed his mind and examined him orally instead of giving a written exam
sections.content_en:
Krznarić is now in his fourth year. He passed Hebrew, Latin, Greek, and “all those philosophies.” He emphasizes that he does not speak “rationally,” but from a relationship with God, and shares a series of anecdotes from exams:

- **Psychology with Father Mijo Nikić.** Before the Blessed Sacrament he said: “If this is a calling from you, I will get a five, and that is a sign to me that you are with me.” The professor asked him precisely what he knew best and said in the end: “If only regular students studied this well!”
- **Medieval Philosophy.** The required reading consisted of two 500-page books of fine print, which Sandra had brought him from the library, and a course reader of about a hundred pages. The evening before the exam he wanted to revise, but in prayer he felt a calling: “Go to Holy Mass in thanksgiving for the exam you would pass tomorrow.” He went. The next day, in front of the classroom, an unknown student listed five questions that the professor usually asks. Those very questions appeared on the exam, and he never saw that student again.
- **Sociology with Professor Peračković.** He was afraid of the written part with 30 to 40 questions, followed by an oral exam. Before the Blessed Sacrament, he prayed that the professor would examine him only orally. At the exam, the professor picked up the test, looked at it, put it down, and said: “I changed my mind, I will examine you orally.” He received a ten. The next day, the professor wrote him an email saying that he had brought the test, “but couldn't hand it out.” Krznarić replied to him that he had prayed for precisely that, and in the end they exchanged books.
- **Moral Theology.** Two weeks ago, he took an exam insufficiently prepared, because the day before he had given a testimony in a parish, and he could barely see the course reader with its fine print. Out of breath, he arrived by bicycle, after taking it out of his truck, and entered with five straight-A students. The exam lasted about an hour. He received an eight, and the professor told him: “You spoke most according to the spirit.” His colleagues noticed this, and he experienced it as a confirmation.

Along with that, he laughed at the description of his routine: in the evening he drives a truck to Zagreb, reviews the material in silence, and then “like a real student” goes to the faculty by bicycle.

sections.subtitle: Zašto je nestao iz javnosti i dug put do ređenja
sections.screenshot_description: Gost objašnjava žrtvu studiranja uz posao i obitelj
sections.content:
*„Bog je vjeran, i to je ono najbitnije“*, sažima Krznarić. Na fakultet se, kaže, „bacio na glavu“, iako nije mlad ni „posložen“. Ne zna hoće li završiti, ali živi dan po dan: *„Nemam ni jučer, nemam ni sutra, imam danas. I to ti, Bože, hoću dati.“*

To je ujedno i odgovor na voditeljevo pitanje gdje je bio posljednje četiri godine. Studij je toliko zahtjevan da bi se, kaže, trebao baviti samo njime, a on cijeli dan radi, kod kuće ga čeka „masa stvari“, a tu je i društveni život. Mnogo je toga morao „odrezati“.

Nada se da će uz Božju pomoć završiti preostalu godinu studija. Nakon pet godina fakulteta slijede **još tri godine puta prema đakonatu**.

Dodaje i zanimljivost. Kad je krenuo, prijatelj ga je upozorio da đakoni dugo nisu ređeni, možda deset ili više godina, te da se ne može postati đakonom s tjelesnim nedostatkom, „ako ti fali i prst“. Krznarić je odgovorio da vjeruje Gospodinu. Kasnije je doznao da su kanonski propisi promijenjeni, pa i netko s protezom, poput njega, može biti zaređen. Ređenja su ponovno započela i sada je u tijeku jedan ciklus.
sections.subtitle_en: Why he disappeared from the public eye and the long road to ordination
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest explains the sacrifice of studying alongside work and family
sections.content_en:
*"God is faithful, and that is what matters most"*, Krznarić summarizes. He says he "dove headfirst" into university, even though he is neither young nor "settled." He does not know whether he will graduate, but he lives day by day: *"I have neither yesterday, nor do I have tomorrow, I have today. And that, God, I want to give to You."*

That is also the answer to the host's question about where he has been for the past four years. The studies are so demanding that, he says, he should be dealing only with them, yet he works all day, a "mass of things" awaits him at home, and then there is social life. He had to "cut off" a lot of it.

He hopes that, with God's help, he will finish the remaining year of studies. After five years of university, there follow **another three years of the journey toward the diaconate**.

He also adds an interesting detail. When he started, a friend warned him that deacons had not been ordained for a long time, perhaps ten or more years, and that one cannot become a deacon with a physical defect, "even if you are missing a finger." Krznarić replied that he trusts the Lord. Later, he learned that the canonical regulations had been changed, so even someone with a prosthesis, like him, can be ordained. Ordinations have resumed, and one cycle is currently underway.

sections.subtitle: Što đakon smije, a što ne: od krštenja do supstancijalne promjene
sections.screenshot_description: Gost objašnjava supstancijalnu promjenu na primjeru papira koji izgara u pepeo
sections.content:
Krznarić objašnjava ovlasti đakona nakon završene formacije. Đakon može gotovo sve, osim **pretvorbe na svetoj misi i ispovijedi**, a time ni bolesničkog pomazanja, uz koje obično ide ispovijed. Đakon može:

- krstiti,
- vjenčavati,
- voditi sprovode,
- dijeliti pričest,
- čitati evanđelje,
- pomagati u svemu što župnik odredi.

Kako bi približio pojam pretvorbe, gost se „teološki izražava“. Supstancijalna promjena, kaže, nastaje kad se materija „u jezgri“ pretvori u nešto drugo, primjerice kad zapaljeni papir postane pepeo. Nešto se slično, prema njegovu objašnjenju, događa kad hostija postaje Tijelo Kristovo, a to može samo svećenik.

Voditelj dodaje širi kontekst. Crkva je suočena s **krizom poziva**, a Hrvatska, iako još stoji bolje od drugih zemalja, ne bi se smjela opustiti. Trajni đakonat vidi kao način da se pozivi ojačaju i da Crkva bude prisutnija. Gostu poručuje da je „na pola puta“ i da vjeruje kako će ga „izgurati do kraja“.
sections.subtitle_en: What a deacon may and may not do: from baptism to substantial change
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest explains substantial change using the example of paper burning into ash
sections.content_en:
Krznarić explains the faculties of a deacon after completing formation. A deacon can do almost everything, except for **consecration at Holy Mass and confession**, and therefore neither anointing of the sick, which usually goes along with confession. A deacon can:

- baptize,
- celebrate marriages,
- conduct funerals,
- distribute Communion,
- read the Gospel,
- assist in everything the pastor assigns.

In order to explain the concept of consecration, the guest "expresses himself theologically." Substantial change, he says, occurs when matter "at its core" transforms into something else, for example when burning paper becomes ash. Something similar, according to his explanation, happens when the host becomes the Body of Christ, and only a priest can do that.

The host adds broader context. The Church is facing a **crisis of vocations**, and Croatia, although still doing better than other countries, should not become complacent. He sees the permanent diaconate as a way to strengthen vocations and make the Church more present. He tells the guest that he is "halfway there" and that he believes he will "push it through to the end."

sections.subtitle: „Ne ‚Bože, daj‘, nego ‚Bože, evo me‘“: poruka onima koji osjećaju poziv
sections.screenshot_description: Gost poziva na molitvu „Bože, evo me, tu sam“
sections.content:
Na kraju razgovora voditelj traži riječi ohrabrenja za one koji razmišljaju o trajnom đakonatu. Krznarić spominje prijatelja s **desetero djece** koji je također dobio poziv. Taj prijatelj dobro poznaje iste strahove: hoće li to moći, sramotu iz djetinjstva kad te profesor prozove pred ploču i pitanje kako se sramotiti s pedeset godina. Unatoč tome, redovito studira i „sve rješava“.

Bog, kaže gost, ne gleda jesi li mehaničar, vozač ili imaš dva fakulteta, nego srce, vjernost i odanost. Govori i o žrtvi:

> *„Kad ideš bliže Bogu, ideš bliže križu… Koliko si više spreman na žrtvu, toliko si više upotrebljiv za Boga.“*

Bog nas, prema njegovim riječima, često „izresetira“, uzme staro i „stavi novo odijelo“, pa čovjek zna da više nije svoj, nego Njegov.

Kao primjer navodi svoje subote. S nekolicinom prijatelja odlazi u kapelicu trajnog klanjanja kod franjevaca u **Varaždinu** od šest do sedam ujutro, zatim na misu i na molitvu krunice na koljenima. U nedjelju je opet na klanjanju u šest. Taj „komadić sna“ smatra malom žrtvom za Gospodina, jer „u Gospodinu ili sabireš ili rasipaš“.

Ključno je, zaključuje, odmaknuti se od molitve **„Bože, daj“** prema molitvi **„Bože, evo me, tu sam. Idem kamo ti želiš“**. Bog čeka naš „da“ i računa na nas.
sections.subtitle_en: "Not 'God, give', but 'God, here I am'": a message to those who feel a calling
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest calls for the prayer "God, here I am, I am here"
sections.content_en:
At the end of the conversation, the host asks for words of encouragement for those who are considering the permanent diaconate. Krznarić mentions a friend with **ten children** who also received a calling. That friend knows well the same fears: whether he will be able to do it, the childhood shame when the teacher calls you up to the blackboard, and the question of how to embarrass oneself at fifty years of age. Despite this, he regularly studies and "handles everything".

God, says the guest, does not look at whether you are a mechanic, a driver, or have two college degrees, but at the heart, fidelity, and devotion. He also speaks about sacrifice:

> *"When you go closer to God, you go closer to the cross… The more you are ready for sacrifice, the more useful you are for God."*

According to his words, God often "resets" us, takes away the old and "puts on a new suit", so a person knows that he is no longer his own, but His.

As an example, he mentions his Saturdays. With a few friends, he goes to the chapel of perpetual adoration at the Franciscans in **Varaždin** from six to seven in the morning, then to Mass and to the prayer of the Rosary on their knees. On Sunday, he is at adoration again at six. He considers that "piece of sleep" a small sacrifice for the Lord, because "in the Lord you either gather or scatter".

It is crucial, he concludes, to move away from the prayer **"God, give"** toward the prayer **"God, here I am, I am here. I am going where you want"**. God is waiting for our "yes" and is counting on us.

sections.subtitle: Blic pitanja: tišina umjesto dvorane, poziv umjesto straha od neuspjeha
sections.screenshot_description: Gost odgovara na blic pitanja u formatu „ili-ili“
sections.content:
Voditelj zatim gosta „rešeta kao pravog studenta“ blic pitanjima u formatu „ili-ili“. Krznarić ga u šali moli da ne pita ništa iz teologije.

- **Život prije ili poslije obraćenja?** „Apsolutno poslije obraćenja.“ Voditelj zaključuje: „Dvojka osigurana.“
- **Tišina i molitva ili svjedočenje pred punom dvoranom?** Tišina i molitva. Sve više „bježi od ljudi“, a na podcast je došao samo zato što mu je Gospodin u molitvi rekao da ide. Inače bi, priznaje, odbio poziv.
- **Teži križ ili veće poslanje?** Nakon duge stanke odgovara da bi pitao Gospodina i da je spreman na oboje. Unutarnji glas ne smatra svojim posjedom, nego nezasluženom milošću, i ne dobiva uvijek odgovor.
- **Biti nepoznat ili javno svjedočiti?** „Lakše je biti nepoznat, ali ako treba, svjedočio bih javno. To ima svoju cijenu i spreman sam je platiti.“
- **Strah od neuspjeha ili strah od propuštenog poziva?** Radije bi se odazvao Gospodinu. Neuspjeha se ne boji, jer je on „sastavni dio uspjeha“: tko ne padne, ne može rasti.
sections.subtitle_en: Quick-fire questions: silence instead of a hall, calling instead of fear of failure
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest answers quick-fire questions in an "either-or" format
sections.content_en:
The host then "grills the guest like a real student" with quick-fire questions in an "either-or" format. Krznarić jokingly asks him not to ask anything from theology.

- **Life before or after conversion?** "Absolutely after conversion." The host concludes: "A passing grade secured."
- **Silence and prayer or witnessing in front of a full hall?** Silence and prayer. He is increasingly "running away from people," and he came to the podcast only because the Lord told him in prayer to go. Otherwise, he admits, he would have declined the invitation.
- **A heavier cross or a greater mission?** After a long pause, he replies that he would ask the Lord and that he is ready for both. He does not consider the inner voice his possession, but an unmerited grace, and he does not always receive an answer.
- **Being unknown or witnessing publicly?** "It is easier to be unknown, but if necessary, I would witness publicly. That comes at a price and I am ready to pay it."
- **Fear of failure or fear of a missed calling?** He would rather respond to the Lord. He is not afraid of failure, because it is an "integral part of success": whoever does not fall cannot grow.

sections.subtitle: Blagoslov na rastanku i najava sljedeće Redefinicije
sections.screenshot_description: Gost na kraju razgovora zaziva Božji blagoslov na obitelji
sections.content:
Voditelj zahvaljuje Krznariću što se odazvao i pozivu i podcastu te zaziva blagoslov na njega, njegovu obitelj, poziv, ispite i studij. Gost uzvraća molitvom: *„Neka dragi Bog blagoslovi, čuva nas, naše obitelji, naše planove, misli, da budemo njegovi. Amen.“*

Voditelj poziva gledatelje da lajkaju, dijele i pretplate se na kanal te da prate profil na **Patreonu**, gdje se sljedeća epizoda može pogledati odmah.

U najavi sljedeće epizode sugovornik iznosi provokativnu misao. Čovječanstvo, kaže, ne zna da Bog postoji jer se katolici, umjesto da se mole na javnim mjestima i napuste svaki položaj koji je u suprotnosti s vjerom, skrivaju kad se mole i pričešćuju se „kad nitko nije u crkvi“.
sections.subtitle_en: Parting blessing and announcement of the next Redefinicija
sections.screenshot_description_en: At the end of the conversation, the guest invokes God's blessing upon families
sections.content_en:
The host thanks Krznarić for responding to both the calling and the podcast and invokes a blessing upon him, his family, calling, exams, and studies. The guest responds with a prayer: *"May dear God bless, protect us, our families, our plans, thoughts, so that we may be His. Amen."*

The host invites viewers to like, share, and subscribe to the channel and to follow the profile on **Patreon**, where the next episode can be watched immediately.

In the preview of the next episode, the interlocutor presents a provocative thought. Humanity, he says, does not know that God exists because Catholics, instead of praying in public places and abandoning every position that is contrary to the faith, hide when they pray and receive Communion "when no one is in the church".

iterations.theme_en: Zlatko Krznarić: from conversion and a fatal accident to the book 'You Are a Witness' and the call to the permanent diaconate
